clue.text: Cited many changes that could be deliberately misleading

definitions.note: a quality of being deliberately misleading, the noun behind the adjective phrase

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quotes lots of alterations that might be meant to deceive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the nine letters of CITED MANY; 'that could be' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is untruthfulness, the habit of telling lies to deceive others on purpose.

clue.text: Expire, though previously fit as a fiddle

parts.note: ex- means former or previous, as in ex-wife
hale means healthy and robust

explanation.surface: Someone dies even though they used to be in perfect health.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire can mean to breathe out, the literal sense of the Latin word.

clue.text: Get soaked and find a medico in French religious house

parts.note: a medico is a doctor, abbreviated Dr
en is the French word for in
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone gets caught in the rain and finds a doctor in a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench is to make thoroughly wet, an imperative synonym for getting something soaked.

clue.text: The payoff for numbers holding Peruvian capital

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: CX is 110 in Roman numerals, a number written in letters
Lima is the capital city of Peru

explanation.surface: Sums of money paid out include some from Peru's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The climax of a story is its culminating moment, the payoff that everything has built towards.

clue.text: Dallied and flirted outrageously

indicators.note: outrageously suggests the letters of the word beside it are behaving wildly and get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone toyed with a lover and flirted shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have trifled is to have toyed or played about idly, the same as having dallied.

clue.text: Skeleton service!

parts.note: read as a fine tea or dinner set whose material is made with the ash of animal skeletons

explanation.surface: A ghoulish picture of a dinner set made of skeletons, or a skeleton staff of servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain tableware made with bone ash, so a whole dinner service of it is literally part skeleton.

clue.text: Leave to enter a plea of guilty

definitions.meaning: permission to be let in, as on an entry ticket
a confession, owning up to an offence

explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both being allowed entry and confessing to wrongdoing.

clue.text: He keeps quiet about the waiter

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning
a server is a waiter at table

explanation.surface: A man stays silent on the subject of the restaurant waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserver is one who keeps or saves something, matching the descriptive phrase.

clue.text: Might set about small daughter with cosmetic

indicators.note: set about means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: might means power or strength
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, a small form of the word

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone would lay into their young daughter over make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'attack' in the surface; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Face powder is a cosmetic dusted on the skin.

clue.text: Complaint when hip belt is adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suffers discomfort whenever their belt round the hips is moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlebitis is inflammation of a vein, a medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: Note the girl appears lax

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A message reveals that a young woman seems careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless in duty, a synonym for lax.

clue.text: Odious creatures dressed in black may well be cut

indicators.note: dressed in means the second piece is clothed by the first

parts.note: sable is the heraldic term for black
lice are parasitic insects, hardly lovable creatures

explanation.surface: Nasty vermin in mourning clothes deserve to be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sliceable is able to be cut into slices, so it may well be cut.

clue.text: The horse gets a drink afterwards

definitions.meaning: a steeplechase horse that races over fences
a drink taken after another, such as a beer after a whisky

explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is both a jump-racing horse and a drink taken to follow another.

clue.text: A great liking for disorder

definitions.meaning: fondness or warm attachment to someone
an older medical sense: a disease or condition affecting part of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Affection means fondness, and in medical usage a disease or disorder of an organ.

clue.text: The astronomer is such a dreamy individual!

definitions.meaning: someone who looks at the stars professionally
a daydreamer with head in the clouds, idealistic and impractical

explanation.definitionFit: A stargazer is literally an astronomer and figuratively an impractical dreamer.

clue.text: Figure there are soldiers about to get involved

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
c is circa, Latin for about
to tangle with someone is to get involved with them

explanation.surface: A number of soldiers are on the point of joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided geometric figure with right angles.

clue.text: A woman from over the sea — Danish maybe

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian lady has come from across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'seA DAnish'; 'over the' and 'maybe' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a woman's first name, a crossword-favourite example of a female name.

clue.text: Tot worrying Dad

indicators.note: worrying suggests disturbing the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A small child is troubling their father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child; it is the verb, as in tot up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot, as in tot up, is to add figures together.

clue.text: One has to run right away

indicators.note: away means the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to race is to run fast

explanation.surface: Someone must dash off immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'at once'; here 'right' is R and 'away' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one on a playing card or die, the single pip.

clue.text: Stout leader, but a fool

parts.note: stout means fat or portly
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A portly boss who is nonetheless an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, a colloquial word for an idiot or fool.

clue.text: To read alone can bring solace

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read carefully
sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: Reading in solitude can be comforting.
explanation.definitionFit: To console is to comfort someone in distress, to bring them solace.

clue.text: German article used in coin production

definitions.meaning: the feminine form of the German definite article, meaning 'the'
a stamping tool that strikes the design onto coins

explanation.definitionFit: Die is a German word for the, and a die is a metal stamp for minting coins.

clue.text: Country music composer

definitions.meaning: John ..., an English composer of the early twentieth century

explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation and also the surname of the English composer John Ireland.

clue.text: Mistakes are reversed — the traitor's held

indicators.note: held means the second piece is held inside the first
reversed means the letters of the word are read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Errors are turned back, and the betrayer is captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like a verb in the surface but is fodder; 'reversed' makes ERA, which then holds the informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially a list of printing mistakes in a book.

clue.text: A tense assembly of politicians

indicators.note: assembly of says the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nervous gathering of lawmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative body made up of politicians.

clue.text: 'Studies at Oxford?', the old monarch scoffs

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George, a past monarch
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A former king mocks the idea of academic study at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford name for the classics degree course; 'scoffs' looks like mocking but means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Greats is the Oxford University name for its course in classics and philosophy.

clue.text: The person who's learned a vehicle may be parked in the street

indicators.note: parked in means the vehicle is put inside the street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone with knowledge leaves their van on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a scholar of deep knowledge.

clue.text: Receives sound information in actual practice

indicators.note: in means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: real means actual or genuine
to hear is to receive information through sound

explanation.surface: Someone takes in what they hear during a live trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice session before a performance.

clue.text: Schools transport

definitions.meaning: railway carriages pulled by a locomotive

explanation.definitionFit: To train is to school or teach, and trains are a rail transport system.

clue.text: Language for two-way communication?

indicators.note: two-way suggests a word that reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Which tongue is used for dialogue in both directions?
explanation.walkthrough: Malayalam, spoken in Kerala in southern India, is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam is the Dravidian language spoken in the Indian state of Kerala.

clue.text: Taking exercise inside, but not in private

indicators.note: inside means the exercise letters go within the other piece

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone works out indoors, but not behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Openly means publicly, the opposite of privately.

clue.text: Diets vary unfortunately when life is hard

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters fall out badly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Diets fluctuate unluckily during tough times.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, a state in which life is difficult.
